fields.name: Harbor
fields.description: A field-notes app that keeps working with no signal and syncs when the tide comes back in.

fields.audience: Researchers and surveyors who take notes outdoors
fields.problem: Note apps assume a connection. In the field they lose entries, or hold up work waiting for sync.
fields.goal: Capture a note in under three seconds anywhere, and never lose one.

fields.ownership: Designed and built it end to end: interface, local store and sync.

fields.approach: Local-first: every write lands in an on-device store, and a background queue replays it to the server.
fields.tools: TypeScript, IndexedDB, a small service worker, Playwright for the offline tests.
fields.decisions:
Last-writer-wins per field, not per note, because two people rarely edit the same sentence.
Plain text first; attachments are a later layer.

fields.challenge: Two devices edit the same note while both are offline.
fields.solution: Merge by field with a visible history, so nothing is silently overwritten.
fields.tradeoff: More bookkeeping per note, in exchange for never losing an edit.

fields.result: Notes save in about 40 ms offline and sync within seconds of reconnecting.
fields.evidence: A scripted airplane-mode test suite and a two-week field trial with three testers.
fields.limitations: Three testers is a small sample, and no one tested on very slow networks.

fields.learned: Conflict rules belong in the first design doc, not after launch.
fields.next_steps: Attachments, and a shared read-only link for collaborators.
